Field NotesOf His Character & Comportment

Mojo spent his formative years as Cairo’s most wanted domestic menace, a period researchers now refer to as “The Dark Epoch” (2016–2021). Following an inexplicable reformation at age five, the specimen emerged as a creature of profound gentleness and unwavering loyalty. He maintains a curated toy collection — one blue ball, one blue bone, one red bone — and has been observed attempting to carry all three simultaneously, an act scientists believe is rooted in abundance anxiety. He is considered the household’s emotional anchor.

Field NotesOf His Character & Comportment

The French Bulldog known as Benji presents as a creature of remarkable composure — regal, introspective, almost disturbingly human in his mannerisms. However, researchers have documented sudden and violent transitions into what is locally termed “the zoomies,” during which all social norms are abandoned and foreign objects are consumed indiscriminately. Benji produces no audible flatulent warning prior to olfactory events, which are classified as a household hazard. He is also known to mount Specimen N°1 without provocation, an act which Mojo endures with characteristic grace.

A Treatise upon Coexistence

On the Peculiar Symbiosis of Two Cairo Specimens

The cohabitation of Specimen N°1 and Specimen N°2 presents to the naturalist a study in contrast rarely afforded within a single household. The elder, Mojo, occupies the role of gentle statesman: a creature of measured temperament whose reformation from his earlier menace has rendered him the steadying axis about which all domestic life revolves. He suffers indignity without complaint and surrenders the choicest resting places with a magnanimity bordering upon the saintly.

The younger, Benji, is by every available measure his ward — beloved, exasperating, and chaotic in equal proportion. He alternates without warning between an almost human stillness and episodes of frenzied locomotion, and his nocturnal respirations have been recorded at volumes sufficient to disturb the furnishings. The household tolerates these afflictions as one tolerates the eccentricities of a brilliant but undisciplined nephew.

It must be noted, in the dispassionate interest of science, that Benji is given to mounting his elder without apparent cause or seasonal pretext. Specimen N°1 receives these advances with the same equanimity he extends to all of life’s indignities, neither encouraging nor resisting, and the matter passes. The researchers conclude that theirs is a stable and affectionate union: one elder, one ward, and a quantity of mutual devotion that no instrument has yet been calibrated to measure.
